title: EchoNext: detecting structural heart disease from ECGs with AI
summary: EchoNext was trained on more than one million heart-rhythm and imaging records to detect structural heart disease. The journal abstract reports internal and external validation, a controlled comparison outperforming cardiologists, and prospective clinical-trial evaluation in patients without previous cardiac imaging that identified undiagnosed disease. This supports a screening study, not proof that deployment improves patient outcomes. The authors also released model weights and an annotated dataset.

evidence.tested: Internal/external diagnostic validation, a controlled cardiologist comparison and prospective clinical-trial screening of patients without previous cardiac imaging.
evidence.unknown: Abstract and publication metadata reviewed. No claim of mortality reduction, universal clinical generalization or independent replication is made.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model estimated structural-heart-disease risk from electrocardiograms to guide imaging-based screening.
